name: seven-kingdoms
desc: Real-time strategy game developed by Trevor Chan of Enlight Software
why: A classic 1990s real-time strategy game with a cult following, a strange old-school pick, though it's a GUI game.

brief.what_it_is: Seven Kingdoms is a real-time strategy game of empire building, originally designed by Trevor Chan and now freely available and maintained by the community. Players compete against up to six AI opponents or other human players for land, trade, and peasants. You start with a single modest village and choose one of seven civilizations (Chinese, Persians, Japanese, Greeks, Normans, Vikings, or Mayans). The homepage describes diplomacy, espionage, mining and manufacturing, markets and trade routes, research of weapons, and magic that can summon the gods. It is a desktop GUI game, not a command-line tool; the brew executable is 7kaa.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a free, community-maintained continuation of Trevor Chan's original game: "Designed by Trevor Chan, now freely available and maintained by the community." It is pitched as an open-ended game of "intrigue and diplomacy, of trade, conquest, and espionage."
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers a download button for version 2.15.7 and says the game is compatible with Windows, macOS and Linux. Downloads and source are hosted on SourceForge; the site says the project moved its files and git repository there and that the GitHub page is wound down. The 2025 news post mentions an experimental Linux build that can be downloaded and run locally, with an installer possibly coming later. Multiplayer needs matching versions, and the forum now asks users to log in. I did not find install steps or a README beyond the homepage, so I cannot confirm dependencies such as SDL from the brew formula side.
brief.standout: It is an open-source-style revival of a 1990s strategy game, still getting AI and multiplayer updates in 2025. The AI work (smarter management, continuing assaults, sea missions) is the recent focus, and the game is built on SDL.
brief.status: maintained: the homepage lists release v2.15.7 with news posted 2025-07-25, after v2.15.6 in 2023-09-02. The 2025 post describes ongoing AI work and a new experimental Linux build.
brief.caveats: The brew desc calls it a real-time strategy game and the scout note calls it a GUI game, so there is no CLI to demo. The homepage was reachable but the text I got contained no GitHub repo or README; the sourceforge project URL I guessed returned 404, so I could not read install or usage docs. The Linux build is labelled experimental. The 2023 news item says a GitHub page is being wound down, so a GitHub README may be stale or missing. Licence was not stated in what I read.
